title: Revelation requires study before asking, not asking alone
setting: Earlier in April 1829, revelations had promised Oliver Cowdery a gift to translate. He tried at Harmony, Pennsylvania, and did not succeed. This revelation, likely given in the second half of April, explained why. It told him to keep writing for Joseph Smith for now. It also promised he would help translate other records later.
summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery to keep writing for Joseph Smith until this record is finished. It promises other records he will later help translate. It says the privilege was taken away because he did not continue as he began. He had supposed it would be given when he only asked. He must study it out in his mind and then ask if it is right. If it is right, his bosom will burn; if not, he will have a stupor of thought. It says he feared, and the time for him to translate has passed. It ends by telling him to stand fast in the work he was called to do.

contextNote.title: Study first, then ask
contextNote.text: Oliver’s attempt to translate failed, and verse 7 names the reason. He had taken “no thought save it was to ask” the Lord. Verse 8 gives the missing step: “study it out in your mind” first. Only then does he ask whether it is right. The answer comes as a burning in the bosom, or as a “stupor of thought” in verse 9. Verse 11 adds a second cause, saying simply that “you feared” when the time came. In this section, asking is the last step of a process that starts with effort.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 6–9 uses verses 7–9 to teach how the Holy Ghost speaks. What does verse 8 ask Oliver to do before he asks, and how could you do that with a decision you face now?
reviewNote: Read all 14 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, April 1829, through Joseph Smith to Oliver Cowdery, urging him to keep writing rather than translate. JSP historical introduction read for the failed attempt and the likely second-half-of-April date. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
